questions.question: How long does a station last on batteries when it measures every ten minutes?
questions.reference: About 14 months on two 18650 cells (accelerated simulation).
questions.answer:
I couldn't find a battery-life figure for a station measuring every ten minutes in Flux. Several people asked whether anyone had measured the battery sleep current, and I found no answer to that question. Those threads are in the Czujniki space, for example [1] and [2].

The reporting interval has also changed between firmware versions, from 24 minutes to 5 minutes, so any estimate depends on the version. Battery problems were reported too: a station at Gdynia was silent for 40 hours in June [3]. Its cause isn't recorded in what I found.

To get a real number, someone needs to measure the sleep current on the current firmware and combine it with the active-measurement energy and the battery capacity. Jonas or Piotr would be the people to ask.

input.q: battery station measures every ten minutes
battery lifetime mAh sleep current measured

judge.reason: The answer states no battery-life value (the reference's ~14 months) and says it could not find a figure, offering only related context and suggestions for measuring it.

questions.question: What happened in this space last week, Monday to Sunday?
questions.reference: At least two of three: the fonts were self-hosted and the CDN removed; the newsletter moved from Mailchimp to Brevo; the cookie banner was removed because Plausible needs no consent. Other events of that week may be named too.
questions.answer:
Last week (Mon 2 to Sun 8 November) the thread had 30 messages, mostly short status updates. Jonas Berg and Sarah Mitchell did most of the posting.

- **Performance:** Mobile load times were the main concern. The careers page took 15 seconds on 2 November, and the pricing page took 24 seconds on 6 November. Lighthouse scores were 6 for about, 24 for careers, and 10 then 6 for pricing.
- **Site fixes:** Fonts were self-hosted and the CDN was removed (2 November). The cookie banner was removed because Plausible needs no consent, and legal confirmed this (5 November).
- **Content and structure:** The about page and product page were moved under /product (5 and 6 November). The newsletter moved from Mailchimp to Brevo, with 340 subscribers (4 November).
- **Open issues:** The SEO audit flagged 20, then 12, broken links on the careers page (4–5 November). Cookie text still needed a legal review before launch. The contact form kept catching spam. Staging went down at least once and was redeployed.
- **Proofreading:** Several pages were sent out for proofreading, including the home page, product page and contact page.

judge.reason: The answer states all three reference events (fonts self-hosted and CDN removed, newsletter moved from Mailchimp to Brevo, cookie banner removed because Plausible needs no consent), matching the reference's requirement of at least two, and contradicts none of them.
